title: Where the dark started
paragraphs: The first thing I ever put out in public was a weather app. Two screens, a lot of gradients, and every decision made because it looked right rather than because I could say why. That was April 2024.

What changed after that was the asking why. I kept the eye for the small stuff — the spacing, the weight of a label, the half-second a transition should take — but I stopped treating those as the whole job. The job is the gap between something being usable and something being worth using.

I am still a student, and I still learn most from the projects that fight back. The work in the next room is roughly eighteen months of doing that in public, in the open, where anyone can see the seams.

aside.label: On the wall
aside.text: Van Gogh spent two years in Nuenen painting weavers and peasants in near-black. He had not found colour yet. He was learning to see.
